name: Try-On Video for WooCommerce
author: nikolaychernuha

sections.description:
Try-On shows your clothes on a real body, in every size, without a photo shoot.

A flat photo can’t show how a dress moves or how a jacket sits on the shoulders. Try-On Video for WooCommerce turns
the product photo you already have into a short, looping video of your clothes worn by one of Try-On’s models, and
plays it in your product gallery, in the size and colour the shopper picks.

No studio, no models to book, no theme to edit.

  • Show the fit, not just the fabric. Clothes on a body, moving, show what a flat photo can’t.
  • Cover every size. Women, men, girls and boys, in every size your shop sells; the video changes when the
    shopper changes size or colour.
  • Start from the photos you have. A flat-lay or ghost-mannequin photo works best, and each colour starts from
    its own picture.
  • Keep your theme. The video is a slide of WooCommerce’s own product gallery, muted and looping.
  • Pay only for what you make. Every run shows its cost and your balance before anything is made.

EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO SHOW THE FIT

From one product to your whole catalogue, the work happens inside WooCommerce, on the screens you already use.

  • Pick, confirm, done. Open a product, choose the clothing photo, the colours and sizes, and a shot. The video
    is made in the background and appears in the gallery.
  • Choose the style. Use Try-On’s ready-made shots, or describe a movement, a scene and a framing in your own
    words and save it for next time.
  • Dress the whole look. Show a product worn with other pieces from your store, with “Goes with this” links to
    each.
  • Say who wears it. Tell Try-On who each category is for, or choose Man, Woman, Boy or Girl for one product,
    and the right model and cost show before anything is made. A Google feed’s gender is read too.
  • Make videos in bulk. Select many products in the Products list and make their videos in one run.
  • Match sizes in seconds. Tell the setup wizard which size attribute you use, and Try-On matches your sizes to
    its models, free.

Made for clothing

Try-On makes videos of clothes: T-shirts, shirts, blouses and tops, knitwear, hoodies and sweatshirts, trousers,
jeans, shorts and skirts, dresses and jumpsuits, jackets, coats and blazers.

Not yet: shoes and boots, hats and caps, bags, jewellery and other accessories, swimwear and lingerie. A photo of
one of these is refused, and only its check is charged.

Start free, pay as you grow

Videos are paid in tokens. Start on the free plan: every store gets 30 tokens a month, enough for 5 short
videos, for as long as Try-On is installed, with nothing to renew. Free videos are made at draft quality and carry
the Try-On logo in a corner, and they are yours to publish.

When you need more, buy tokens: you unlock more videos and higher quality, and the videos you make from then on
carry no logo. A photo that can’t be used costs only its check, and so does a video that fails.

Own your videos – forever

Every video is saved in your WordPress media library, exactly as it arrives. Deleting the plugin never deletes them,
and your product pages go back to how they were.

Your storefront never calls Try-On: it plays the video from your own site, and nothing about your shoppers, orders
or customers is ever sent. If you choose to share anonymous usage data with us, you can turn it off at any time.

Translate

Try-On Video for WooCommerce is in English for now. It is ready to be translated, and its screens work
right-to-left; help bring it to your language at
translate.wordpress.org.

Connection to Try-On

The videos are made by Try-On, a paid service operated by ORCA-AD LTD at https://connect.try-on.co. The plugin
can’t make videos without it, and talks to it over HTTPS only. This is what it sends, and when:

  • When you connect: your store’s URL and name, the plugin and WooCommerce versions, and the language you work
    in. That language also goes with every link to Try-On’s pages (your account, buying tokens), so they answer you
    in it.
  • Right after connecting, and on a wp-admin page while one is missing: it reads Try-On’s prices, options, models
    and movements, and downloads the models’ pictures and the movements’ previews into your site’s uploads folder.
  • Every request carries the plugin’s version, and every request made once connected also carries your store’s
    URL. Try-On’s answer about your account says when a newer version of the plugin is out, for the update notice.
  • While connecting, Try-On calls your store back once at /wp-json/tryon-video/v1/connect/ownership to confirm
    the store holds the request being approved. The store answers only for a request one of its managers started.
  • When you set up sizes, once connected, so Try-On can suggest which attribute is your size and which your
    colour: for each variation attribute, its slug and name, its type, how many products use it, up to 50 of its
    values, and whether your pictures change with it.
  • When you match sizes: the size attribute’s name and your size names.
  • While you build an outfit in Configure: the product and up to 100 products you might add to its outfit, each
    as its product id and, when the store has them, its item type and kind, plus the ids of the pictures the outfit
    already wears, so Try-On can say which pieces it can make.
  • When you save a shot in your own words: the words, the language they are written in, and, if you ask for one,
    a preview to film, at the tokens shown.
  • When you confirm a run, and only then: the clothing photo you picked, the model, the size, any words you wrote,
    the quality and length, your store URL, your language, and an anonymous code for the staff member who started it.
  • When you ask what goes with a product, or with the products you select in the Products list: each product’s
    pictures, title, categories and attributes, at the tokens shown.
  • When you change two-factor in Account & spending: whether everyone on your Try-On account must use it to
    sign in.
  • When you send an error report, only then and after you have seen it: the error, the plugin’s recent activity,
    its settings’ ids and switches (never words you typed), your active plugins and theme with their versions, your
    store’s setup (WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP versions, language, memory and upload limits, whether its scheduled
    tasks run), and the note you add.
  • The finished video is downloaded from the address the service returns.
  • Anonymous usage data, only if you turn it on (off by default): once a day, the WordPress, PHP, WooCommerce and
    plugin versions, the site language, and whether steps such as connecting or making a video worked. No store URL,
    no ids, nothing about your shoppers.

This service is provided by ORCA-AD LTD: Terms of use, Privacy policy.
sections.installation:
Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 7.0 or greater
  • WooCommerce 11.0 or greater
  • PHP 8.1 or greater
  • A Try-On account: free to create, with tokens every month

Automatic installation

Automatic installation is the easiest option: WordPress handles the file transfer, and you won’t need to leave your
web browser. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active, then go to Plugins → Add Plugin, search for
“Try-On Video for WooCommerce”, and click Install Now, then Activate.

Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Try-On and click Connect. The setup wizard then asks which size
attribute your shop uses, which sizes matter and how long the videos should be; you can change every answer later.

Manual installation

Download the plugin’s zip, upload it under Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin, activate it, then
connect your store in WooCommerce → Settings → Try-On.

Updating

Automatic updates should work smoothly; we still recommend you back up your site. Your videos, settings and
connection are kept across updates.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Try-On account?

Yes. The videos are made by Try-On, so you connect your store once, from WooCommerce → Settings → Try-On.
Connecting is free, and every account gets tokens each month, so you can make a finished video before paying
anything.

What can I make videos of?

Clothes worn on the body: tops, shirts, knitwear and hoodies, trousers, jeans, shorts and skirts, dresses and
jumpsuits, jackets, coats and blazers. Shoes and boots, hats and caps, bags, jewellery and other accessories,
swimwear and lingerie aren’t supported yet: a photo of one of these is refused, and only its check is charged. The
plugin shows the full list where you choose what to make.

Where can I get help?

Ask in the plugin’s support forum. The plugin
also has a guided tour of every screen.

Which photos work best?

A photo of the clothing on its own: a flat-lay or a ghost mannequin. A picture with a person in it is refused, and
its check is still charged. For the back, add a photo of the back to the product’s gallery.

Does the plugin pick the clothing photo for me?

No, you always choose. A colour whose variations already have a picture starts with that picture, and you can change
it. Only when you make videos for many products at once, and agree to it, does Try-On pick each product’s picture.

Will it work with my theme?

Yes, with any theme that shows WooCommerce’s standard product gallery. The video is added as one of its slides.

Will it slow down my product pages?

No. Your storefront never calls Try-On: it plays a video file from your own media library, and only the video on
show loads.

Which sizes appear?

The ones your shop already sells. Try-On matches each of your sizes to one of its own, and you can change any match
under Products → Attributes.

Can I use my own model photos?

No. The videos show Try-On’s own models, in every size; you choose the clothing photo.

What happens to my videos if I delete the plugin?

They stay in your media library: deleting the plugin never deletes the videos you paid for. Installing it again
brings them back to your products.

My videos are waiting. What do I do?

WordPress runs background work when someone visits your site, so on a quiet shop a video can wait. The plugin tells
you when nothing has run for fifteen minutes. Ask your host to run WordPress’s scheduler every minute (a “cron
job”) to fix it for good. Nothing is lost while a video waits.

Where is the source code?

In the plugin itself: every script ships with the TypeScript it is built from, and npm ci && npm run build builds
them again.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

Try-On 1.0.1 dresses your models in whole outfits and makes every choice easier to see before you pay for it. A video can now show up to two pieces, such as a jacket over a shirt and trousers: Configure suggests only the pieces Try-On can make, refuses an outfit that can’t be worn together before any tokens are held, and shows any outer-layer charge in the price first. Movements are chosen from tiles that play when you hover and open large when you click, each showing the model its preview is made on, and shots in your own words are written in one window with a preview filmed for the tokens shown. There is one catwalk now, the model walking in from afar, and stores that used the near catwalk move to it while their finished videos keep playing. Videos come in Standard and Premium, with Premium the default until you choose; only the qualities your account can order are offered, and a shot Try-On no longer makes is greyed out instead of failing later. The setup opens inside wp-admin, larger, with the storefront’s AI label shown on an example picture, picks up where you left it, never holds back a store already in use, and ends on your products ready to plan videos or take the tour. A newly connected store has Try-On’s prices, movements and models straight away. Connecting explains a refusal, and a store another Try-On account still held can connect again once Try-On has checked it at its own address. Disconnecting says first what happens to videos still being made, deleting the plugin with Remove everything also disconnects the store, and Try-On tells you when a newer version is out. Every movement, scene, framing and pose is translated, alongside many smaller fixes to the setup, the product box and the shot lists.

1.0.0

  • First release.
